content: {"summary":"When a pod shows ~70% throttled periods but modest average CPU, look at the throttling ratio, CPU‑stat counters and the process thread count. A high throttling ratio (>25% periods) together with a thread‑count that exceeds the container’s CPU limit (e.g., GOMAXPROCS or gunicorn workers set to the node core count) points to a thread‑count mismatch rather than genuine load.","likely_cause":"Thread‑count mismatch (container limit lower than the number of active threads/workers) causing CFS throttling","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"High throttling periods with low average CPU indicate CFS throttling, not real load","evidence_ids":["RB-002#0","RB-002#1"],"quote":"If a service's p99 latency climbs while its CPU graph looks comfortable, suspect CFS throttling before anything else."},{"text":"A throttling ratio above ~25% of periods is a strong sign of quota exhaustion","evidence_ids":["RB-002#1"],"quote":"Anything above roughly 25% of periods during the incident is a strong sign."},{"text":"Thread‑count sized to the node instead of the container is the usual trigger for throttling","evidence_ids":["RB-002#2"],"quote":"The usual trigger is a thread count sized to the node instead of the container."}],"next_checks":["Check the Grafana panel \"container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total / container_cpu_cfs_periods_total\" for >25% throttled periods","Run `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.stat` twice and compare nr_throttled/nr_periods and throttled_usec growth","Inspect GOMAXPROCS inside the pod (or WEB_CONCURRENCY for gunicorn) to ensure it does not exceed the pod's CPU limit","List top threads (e.g., `kubectl exec ... top -H -p 1`) and verify the number of busy threads matches the limit","If mismatch found, adjust GOMAXPROCS or worker count and redeploy the pod"]}
